Climate Crisis | Representative Casar Skip to main content 446 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20003 Email Me (202) 225-5645 Climate Crisis Image The climate crisis is real. In Texas, we’ve seen the impacts first-hand: from Winter Storm Uri, to historic floods, to wildfires, and so much more. Texans have taken care of each other through these crises, but we can’t afford to rely on local and individual solutions any longer. I’m a proud co-sponsor of the Green New Deal and similar legislation to create good union jobs in clean energy and protect communities harmed by pollution and natural disasters. Our country can and must take care of everyone along the way — from children to seniors to fossil fuel workers. Economy | Representative Casar Skip to main content 446 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20003 Email Me (202) 225-5645 Economy Image From East Austin to West San Antonio, Texas’s 35th Congressional District is home to hardworking families of all backgrounds. But today, too many Texans are struggling to afford the basic necessities while big corporations make record profits. Congress must ensure that the ultra rich pay their fair share in taxes and contribute to the schools, roads, and community services that we all use. I support legislation to address skyrocketing rent and mortgage rates, end discriminatory policies that prevent Texans from becoming homeowners, and expand public housing. I’m also fighting to protect veterans, older Americans, students and consumers from predatory business tactics, through legislation such as the End Junk Fees for Renters Act . Education | Representative Casar Skip to main content 446 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20003 Email Me (202) 225-5645 Education Image Texas’s Congressional District 35 is filled with many diverse school districts and is home to higher education institutions — including Hispanic Serving Institutions (HSIs) and Historically Black Universities (HBCUs). Thousands of students attend school in hopes of achieving their academic goals. In Congress, I’m working for students by pushing for policies that increase funding for education at all levels, support our teachers and school staff, and ensure that every student can receive a high-quality education. We also must focus on investing in and supporting our teachers and school staff. I support erasing student debt and making community colleges and public universities free. Child Care | Representative Casar Skip to main content 446 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20003 Email Me (202) 225-5645 Child Care Image It’s time for Congress to provide solutions for families and win truly universal and affordable child care for everyone. I am working to support the learning and growth of children, make sure families can afford high quality child care, and adequately compensate and support child care workers. We can pass legislation that limits child care costs to 7% of any family’s income. Right now, we know Texans spend far, far more than this, and that has to change. I also believe in providing child care to our military families. That’s why I’m the author of an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act that would give the Department of Defense the authority to appropriate funds from programs or weapons that it deems unnecessary to instead fund child care programs for military families. Health Care | Representative Casar Skip to main content 446 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20003 Email Me (202) 225-5645 Health Care Image Fixing our healthcare system is one of my top priorities in Congress. Americans pay more for health care than anyone else in the world, and we still get worse results than other countries. And that’s just for Americans who have access to health care; Texas, meanwhile, has both the largest number and percentage of uninsured residents in the country . Health care should be a right, not a privilege, and it’s time for Congress to guarantee healthcare for all people. I’m a proud co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act , because no Texan should have to skip taking medicine or not see a doctor because they can’t afford it. Congress must ensure that families across the country can afford their prescription drugs and to receive high-quality health care. I also support legislation to protect and strengthen Medicare and Medicaid, and will always oppose efforts to cut funding for these essential programs. Civil Rights | Representative Casar Skip to main content 446 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20003 Email Me (202) 225-5645 Civil Rights Image From East Austin to Hays County down to the West Side of San Antonio, local civil rights and labor rights movements have worked hard to secure progressive policies in our communities. Working Texans have organized to combat discrimination and protect civil rights for all people. Instead of being strengthened or expanded, the civil rights of Texans are under attack by an unethical and unaccountable majority on the Supreme Court. Texas can do better — after all, it was Texas native President Lyndon Baines Johnson who signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and outlawed discrimination on the basis of race, religion, sex, and nationality. Now, we must do more. I support legislation like the Equality Act to enshrine LGBTQIA+ nondiscrimination protections into law, as well as the Justice for All Act to prohibit discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or race-related characteristics.
